oauth.notes: Set up in Google Cloud. The same steps apply to other Google APIs, but Gmail's reading permissions are among the most tightly controlled.

verdict.summary: Creating the app takes minutes, but reading or changing email counts as 'restricted' access. Google must verify your app, and if your servers handle that email, an approved security assessor must audit you every year. Expect weeks.

whoYouNeed.role: Someone who can edit DNS for your company domain
whoYouNeed.why: Google requires proof that you own the domain on your homepage and privacy policy.
The yearly security assessment is done by a third-party assessor. Google does not publish a price.

whoYouNeed.role: A person to record a demo video
whoYouNeed.why: Google wants a video of the sign-in flow and of each restricted permission in use.

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud and create a project
steps.plain: Log in to console.cloud.google.com with a company account and create a project for your app.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in and accepting Google Cloud's terms are yours to do.

steps.title: Turn on the Gmail API
steps.plain: In the project, open the API Library, search for Gmail API and enable it.

steps.title: Set up the consent screen
steps.plain: This is the 'Allow?' page your users will see. Enter your app's name, a support email, and choose 'External' so people outside your company can connect.
steps.technical: Google Auth Platform > Get started. Audience: External (any Google user) or Internal (your Workspace org only). Add your homepage, privacy policy and authorized domains.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.plain: Create a 'Web application' client and paste in the redirect address from your Composio Gmail auth config.
steps.technical: Clients > Create client > Web application. Authorized redirect URIs: the value your Composio auth config shows. Composio's Google guide still shows the older https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

sources.title: Composio: GitHub OAuth guide (notes the v3 address)

evidence.note: Composio's own guides disagree on the redirect address. Use the dashboard value.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.plain: Create a client secret and paste it, with the client ID, into your Composio auth config.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

steps.title: Add test users and try it
steps.plain: While the app is in 'Testing', only people you list can connect, and they see a warning screen. Add your team's emails and try a connection.

steps.title: Prove you own your domain
steps.plain: Verify your company domain in Google Search Console, usually by adding a DNS record.
steps.whyHuman: Needs access to your domain's DNS settings.

steps.title: Publish a privacy policy and record a demo video
steps.plain: Your privacy policy must live on the same domain as your homepage and explain how you use Google data. Record a video showing the sign-in flow and how you use each restricted permission, and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.
steps.whyHuman: The policy is a legal commitment, and the video needs a real walkthrough. An agent can draft both for you to review.

link.label: Open YouTube Studio to upload as Unlisted

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.plain: Fill in the verification form: why you need each restricted permission and why a narrower one won't do. Attach the video link.

steps.title: Google reviews your app
steps.plain: Google checks your branding, then the restricted permissions. Branding takes 2 to 3 business days. The restricted review 'can potentially take several weeks'.

evidence.note: Google says 'several weeks'. The 14 to 42 day range is our reading of that, not a Google number.

steps.title: Security assessment (yearly)
steps.plain: Apps that reach restricted Gmail data through a server, not just the user's browser, need an assessment by a Google-approved assessor. When Composio fetches email for your agent, the data passes through Composio's servers under your app, so expect this to apply. Google's Trust and Safety team contacts you when it's time, and you repeat it every 12 months.
steps.whyHuman: You choose and pay an assessor, and answer their questions.

evidence.note: The requirement and yearly repeat are sourced. That Composio relaying data triggers it for your app is our reading, not confirmed by Google or Composio. Google gives no price or duration; 7 to 30 days is a guess.

forks.effect: Sending is 'sensitive', not 'restricted'. You still need Google's app verification, but no security assessment. This is much faster.

forks.condition: Only people inside your own Google Workspace will connect
forks.effect: Choose 'Internal' on the consent screen. No verification is needed.

forks.condition: You stay unverified (pilot with a few users)
forks.effect: Users see an 'unverified app' warning, and the app is capped at 100 new users in total. Sign-ins in Testing mode also expire sooner.

evidence.note: Google says Testing-mode refresh tokens have limited lifetimes. The commonly quoted 7 days was not re-checked.

nuances.title: Ask for the narrowest Gmail permission
nuances.detail: gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata and full mail access are all restricted. gmail.send is only sensitive. Google asks you to justify why a narrower permission won't work.
nuances.ifStuck: If your agent only drafts or sends, drop the reading permissions to skip the security assessment.

nuances.title: Re-verification every year
nuances.detail: Restricted-scope apps must be reassessed at least every 12 months, and adding a new restricted permission can trigger a new assessment.
nuances.ifStuck: Put the renewal in the calendar the day your approval letter arrives.

nuances.title: Unverified while you wait
nuances.detail: Until approval, you are limited to listed test users or 100 new users behind a warning screen.
nuances.ifStuck: Run pilots with Composio's managed Gmail app (it shows 'Composio' on the consent screen) while your own app is in review.

config.redirectUriNote: Use the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify
scopes.plain: Read, change and delete email (not permanent deletion).

useCases.label: Read, sort or draft replies to email
useCases.summary: Restricted access: Google verification plus a yearly third-party security assessment.

useCases.label: Send email only
useCases.summary: gmail.send is sensitive, not restricted: Google verification but no security assessment.

evidence.note: The scope class is sourced. Google gives no duration for sensitive-scope verification, so the wait is our estimate.

useCases.label: Only people in your own Google Workspace
useCases.summary: Mark the app Internal. No verification needed.

composio.note: You can connect users today with Composio's own Gmail app while yours is set up or in review. Users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, rate limits are shared with other Composio customers, and polling triggers run at most every 15 minutes. Switch to your own app when it is ready. This is the realistic way to pilot Gmail during Google's weeks of review.

existingApp.summary: Add Composio's redirect address to your existing OAuth client, or create a second client in the same project. Either way you keep the verification your project already has, as long as the permissions stay the same.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You add a restricted permission you were not verified for
reReviewTriggers.effect: Google re-verifies the app, and a new restricted scope can require a new security assessment.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You change the app name, logo or domains users see
reReviewTriggers.effect: Brand verification runs again, typically 2 to 3 business days.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: A second client in the same project
reReviewTriggers.effect: It sits under the same consent screen, so it should not need its own verification.

evidence.note: Our reading of how verification attaches to the project's consent screen; not stated outright on the page.

blockers.symptom: Google's automated brand check lists problems
blockers.cause: Your home page must be public (not behind a login), describe the app and link to the privacy policy. The privacy policy must be on the same domain and explain how you use Google data. Your domain must be verified in Google Search Console.
blockers.fix: Fix each listed issue and run verification again, or request a manual review (usually 2 to 3 business days). Cancel verification before changing branding, and publish within 7 days of a passing result.

blockers.cause: Google's Trust & Safety team may email you for more information, and the review pauses until you answer.
blockers.fix: Check the developer contact and support email addresses on your consent screen, including spam. Check the Verification Center for a paused status, and reply on the same email thread.

escalate.label: Google: verification and Trust & Safety follow-up

blockers.symptom: Verification is refused because of a policy flag
blockers.cause: A project on your account was flagged for a Terms of Service violation, or your domain is marked dangerous in Google Search.
blockers.fix: Resolve the flagged project and appeal in the Google Cloud console, or fix the Search Console issues and request a security review. Resubmit only after that review finishes.
